title: Refrigerated vs Frozen Peptide Vial Labels: Specify When You Apply Them
seoTitle: Refrigerated vs Frozen Peptide Vial Labels
description: A vial label that survives cold storage may not adhere when applied to an already frozen vial. Compare the application sequence, thaw cycle and barcode proof before ordering.
alt: AI-generated RP Research vials with complete printed teal and purple labels beside refrigerated and frosted sample racks
caption: AI-generated comparison, not an RP cold-chain test. Fictional RP Research names, lot numbers and expiry dates are illustrative; the pictured labels have no verified storage rating.
intro: The purchasing question is not simply how cold the vial gets. Ask whether the label is applied before cooling or onto an already cold surface.

title: Mixed-Flavor Supplement Sample Kits: Keep Carton and Sachet Identities Aligned
seoTitle: Mixed-Flavor Supplement Sample Kit Label Guide
description: Plan a variety-kit carton and three inner sachet designs as one controlled artwork family. Check flavor count, lot mapping, retail unit and copy approval before printing.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness variety carton with citrus, berry and mint sachets, each with a distinct printed flavor icon and lot block
caption: AI-generated packaging concept, not approved supplement artwork. RP Wellness, flavor icons, barcode and lot codes are fictional; the regulatory copy is deliberately incomplete.
intro: A mixed-flavor kit is not one enlarged sachet design. The carton and each inner unit need a matching identity and a clear sale-unit decision.
related: Decide which copy lives on sticks and cartons
sources: FDA: Dietary Supplement Labeling Guide, Chapter I
FDA: small and multiunit package provisions

title: Amber Dropper Bottle Labels: Proof Oil Residue and Shoulder Clearance
seoTitle: Amber Dropper Bottle Label Adhesion Guide
description: Custom amber dropper labels need more than a good-looking wrap. Check straight-wall height, glass cleanliness, accidental oil contact and real handling before final approval.
alt: AI-generated RP Botanicals amber dropper bottle with finished emerald label beside an unlabelled test bottle and printed label roll
caption: AI-generated RP Botanicals packaging concept. The bottle, 30 mL marking and batch are fictional; no adhesive, oil-resistance or regulatory performance is demonstrated.
intro: Dropper bottles look simple until the label meets a curved shoulder, a wet pipette or an oily hand.
sources: Avery Dennison: neck-label adhesion and bottle surface guide
FDA: Dietary Supplement Labeling Guide, Chapter I

title: Holographic Security Labels on Sheets vs Rolls: Buy for the Application Method
seoTitle: Holographic Security Label Sheets vs Rolls
description: Compare hand-applied holographic sheets with machine-ready rolls. Specify peel direction, liner, gap, unwind and carton-opening placement before ordering.
alt: AI-generated RP Secure holographic seals supplied on a roll and a sheet, with one seal bridging a folding carton flap
caption: AI-generated RP Secure packaging concept. The shiny design does not verify tamper performance; production die-cuts and liner specifications require real samples.
intro: A beautiful hologram can still be the wrong purchase if the packing team cannot dispense it at the planned speed.
sources: HERMA: labels on rolls and machine dispensing

title: Hologram Carton Seals for Returns: What the Receiving Team Can Actually Check
seoTitle: Hologram Carton Seal Return Inspection Guide
description: A return inspection needs a clear pass/fail process, not a shiny sticker alone. Define seam placement, tear evidence, lot records and escalation before specifying hologram seals.
alt: AI-generated RP Secure cartons side by side, one with intact hologram bridge and one opened with a torn seal during receiving inspection
caption: AI-generated return-inspection scenario, not an actual RP security test. A broken seal is an inspection signal, not proof by itself of product authenticity or prior handling.
intro: If a returned carton arrives with a shiny seal, the first question is whether the receiving team knows what an opened one looks like.
sources: GS1: inspection business step and packaging integrity
